messages.text: Leicestershire's points deduction for poor pitch reduced

metadata.summary: Leicestershire’s 27-point deduction for breaching pitch regulations in August's win over Glamorgan has been reduced to 19.
metadata.content: County Championship: Leicestershire have eight points reinstated from 27-point deduction for poor pitch blamed on Bollywood film shoot | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content County Championship: Leicestershire have eight points reinstated from 27-point deduction for poor pitch blamed on Bollywood film shoot Leicestershire chief executive Emma White confirms club will still appeal its deduction for the poor pitch that groundsman Callum Lewis later argued was due to a Bollywood film shoot; they will appeal against decision despite having eight points reinstated from original 27-point deduction Monday 28 September 2026 17:38, UK Image: Leicestershire were relegated following a defeat by champions Warwickshire in the last round of County Championship fixtures Leicestershire’s 27-point deduction for breaching pitch regulations in August's win over Glamorgan has been reduced to 19. The Foxes were relegated from Division One of the County Championship last week following an innings defeat by champions Warwickshire. Leicestershire's groundsman Callum Lewin had argued filming of an unscheduled Bollywood film - believed to be for a biopic of former India captain Sourav Ganguly - had taken place at the ground four days before the Glamorgan fixture between August 20-23, preventing the pitch from being covered for eight hours in bright sunshine and heatwave temperatures. metadata.summary: The United States maintained their Presidents Cup winning streak over the International Team, with the latest victory reigniting debate about whether change is needed in the biennial contest.
metadata.content: Presidents Cup: Does Team USA's comeback win over Internationals show change is needed to make event more competitive? | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Presidents Cup: Does Team USA's comeback win over Internationals show change is needed to make event more competitive? A different format? Fewer points on offer? LIV Golf players involved? Extra team events on the schedule? We look at possible ways to make the Presidents Cup even more competitive, following the United States' record-extending 11th consecutive win over the International Team Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Monday 28 September 2026 12:33, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final day of the Presidents Cup, where Team USA dominated the Sunday singles to close out a comeback victory over the International Team The United States maintained their Presidents Cup winning streak over the International Team, with the latest victory reigniting debate about whether change is needed in the biennial contest. Brandt Snedeker's side produced the largest final-day comeback in Presidents Cup history at Medinah, winning 9.5 of the 12 points on offer in the Sunday singles to close out a record-extending 11th consecutive victory. A 17-13 winning margin doesn't tell the full picture from a closer-than-expected contest, including a foursomes session sweep for the Internationals on Friday and them leading going into the final day for just the fourth time ever. messages.text: Matos on Swansea's fast start and working with Klopp at Liverpool

metadata.summary: It is Swansea City who sit top of the Championship after eight games. Not something many would have expected at the start of the season.
metadata.content: Vitor Matos interview: Swansea City boss on their fast start and working under Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Vitor Matos interview: Swansea City boss on their fast start and working under Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool Vitor Matos speaks to Sky Sports about Swansea City's fast start and working under Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool. Watch Swansea City vs Norwich City live on Sky Sports+ and the Sky Sports app at 12.30pm on Saturday October 10 Simeon Gholam EFL Editor @simeongholam Monday 28 September 2026 11:33, UK It is Swansea City who sit top of the Championship after eight games. Not something many would have expected at the start of the season. But Vitor Matos and his high-pressing, energetic side have enjoyed a wonderful opening to the campaign. It is performances, more than results, that have pleased him. "I'm happy with the start more than the results," Matos - who won Sky Bet Championship Manager of the Month for August - tells Sky Sports . "It's the style and the feeling that when you go to watch us play, you have a good feeling. We are happy when you are out, especially our fans. That's what we wanted, that's what we are trying more than anything. "So far, it's been good." messages.text: Norris apologises for Colapinto comments following Baku crash

metadata.summary: Reigning Formula 1 world champion Lando Norris said he apologised to Franco Colapinto for the stinging comments he made after the Alpine driver caused a crash that took both of them out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lando Norris apologises to Franco Colapinto for critical comments made about Alpine driver following Azerbaijan GP crash | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lando Norris apologises to Franco Colapinto for critical comments made about Alpine driver following Azerbaijan GP crash Franco Colapinto caused a collision with his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris that took all three of them out of the Azerbaijan GP; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia from Friday morning live on Sky Sports F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix Monday 28 September 2026 14:52, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was carnage on the safety car restart after contact between Alpine team-mates resulted in Lando Norris crashing out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix Reigning Formula 1 world champion Lando Norris said he apologised to Franco Colapinto for the stinging comments he made after the Alpine driver caused a crash that took both of them out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Colapinto triggered the accident during a Safety Car restart in Baku when he locked his brakes into the first corner and hit the side of his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly, who was sent straight into Norris' McLaren on his outside. Speaking in the immediate aftermath of the incident in Saturday's race, Norris said "there are some drivers who shouldn't be in Formula 1" and called for such incidents to result in one-race bans for the initiator. messages.text: Why Man City charges case could still drag on for years

metadata.summary: Manchester City have been embroiled in legal disputes with UEFA and the Premier League for 12 years and they are so determined to clear their name, and the 115 charges case is so big, that it could still be years before the saga is concluded.
metadata.content: Man City charges: Case involving alleged breaches of Premier League financial rules could drag on for years | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man City charges: Case involving alleged breaches of Premier League financial rules could drag on for years Sky Sports News understands that the process around Manchester City case is moving to the appeal stage, after reports claimed that most of the charges against the club for breaking Financial Fair Play rules were found to have been proven Kaveh Solhekol Chief Correspondent Monday 28 September 2026 16:59, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol explains why the Premier League has not commented on reports a decision has been reached in the 115 charges case. City insist they have irrefutable evidence to prove they did not break the rules Manchester City have been embroiled in legal disputes with UEFA and the Premier League for 12 years and they are so determined to clear their name, and the 115 charges case is so big, that it could still be years before the saga is concluded. According to reports last week, an independent tribunal has reached decisions in the case and Sky Sports News understands the process is moving to the appeal stage. In 2014, City paid a £49m fine for breaking UEFA's financial fair play (FFP) rules and in 2020 they were given a two-year European competition ban and fined €30m (£25.7m) for breaking the rules again.
